rows.name: Koopa Troopa (green shell, World 1-1)
rows.notes:
World 1-1's one Koopa Troopa, paused while walking left toward Mario (game_mode $0770=1). list_sprites decodes a 6-entry OAM block at slots 18-23, origin (177,185) = top-left of a 16x24 metasprite; every entry is sprite palette 5 (OAM attr $65 -> palette bits 1, flip_h set, behind_background=false, no flip_v). OAM entry order in memory is $A5, $FC(blank), $A7, $A6, $A9, $A8. Entries as (tile id, x/y offset from origin, flips):
- $A5 (165), (+0,+0), flip_h - top-left (shell top/head)
- $FC (252), (+8,+0), flip_h - blank filler (top-right cell of the 16x24 form)
- $A7 (167), (+0,+8), flip_h - middle-left (shell)
- $A6 (166), (+8,+8), flip_h - middle-right (shell)
- $A9 (169), (+0,+16), flip_h - bottom-left (feet)
- $A8 (168), (+8,+16), flip_h - bottom-right (feet)
All from SPRITE pattern table $0000. Sprite palette 5 live = [$0F black, $1A green, $30 white, $27 orange] (green shell + orange/white body). Confirmed by hit-test: list_sprites(185,196) returned OAM index 21 tile $A6 palette 5, opaque (pixel_value 3); get_region object mode at (185,196) = 213 connected sprite-palette-5 pixels using slots 1,2,3 across OAM #18,#20,#21,#22,#23 (CHR $A5,$A6,$A7,$A8,$A9), box (177,186)-(192,208); get_pixel_color(181,190) = $30 white (palette-5 slot 2). REACH (no reference): from the World 1-1 level-start checkpoint (save_state slot 1) write the star timer $079F=200 (nonzero = invincible) then play_input holding right+B in a 30-frame jump cycle ({right,b,a} 18 / {right,b} 12); at the tall pipe (~level x 900) he jams against it, so back off with Left 30 frames, then run {right,b} 12 + jump {right,b,a} 30 and he clears it; stop when $006D/$0086 read page 6 / low 93 (level x = 6*256+93 = 1629), where the Koopa is on screen at x 177 next to Mario (Mario OAM x 113).
rows.why: the green Koopa Troopa at the screen's right edge in this screenshot; OAM $A5 (head) with a $FC filler over $A7/$A6 and $A9/$A8 (shell and feet), all h-flipped: rendered from sprite CHR they are the Koopa facing left, 16x24

rows.name: Starman (star / invincibility power-up)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 starman, forced and paused sitting on the used ? block at level x≈336 (screen origin (186,130)), game_mode $0770=1. list_sprites decodes a 4-entry OAM block at slots 42-45, origin (186,130) = top-left of a 16x16 metasprite; every entry is sprite palette 7 (OAM attrs $23 / $63), behind_background = true, no flip_v, and the right-hand two are flip_h. Entries as (tile id, x/y offset from origin, flips):
- $8D (141), (+0,+0), no flips - upper-left (star point)
- $8D (141), (+8,+0), flip_h (attr $63) - upper-right (mirror of upper-left)
- $E4 (228), (+0,+8), no flips - lower-left (lower star points)
- $E4 (228), (+8,+8), flip_h (attr $63) - lower-right (mirror of lower-left)
So the starman uses only TWO distinct CHR tiles ($8D and $E4), each drawn once plain and once horizontally mirrored, from SPRITE pattern table $0000. Sprite palette 7 live = [$0F,$0F,$36,$17] (slot3 brown = the star body), so it renders brown/black here. Confirmed: get_region object mode at (192,134) = 112 connected sprite-palette-7 pixels using slots 1,3 across OAM #42,#43,#44,#45 (CHR $8D,$E4), box (187,130)-(200,143); get_pixel_color(196,141) = $17 brown; list_sprites(190,134) hit-tested OAM index 42 tile $8D palette 7.
HOW IT WAS MADE TO APPEAR (no reference): the emerging item's TYPE is the zero-page byte $0039. The power-up sprite routine at CPU $E6E2 does LDX $39 and picks one 4-tile group from the PRG table at CPU $E6BE = prgRom 0x66BE: X=0 = $76 $77 $78 $79 (mushroom), X=1 = $D6 $D6 $D9 $D9 (fire flower), X=2 = $8D $8D $E4 $E4 (starman), X=3 = $76..$79 again (other mushroom). The pickup code at CPU $D80C reads $39: <2 = mushroom/flower, 2 = star (LDA #$23 / STA $079F, the star timer), 3 = the other item. REACH: from save_state slot 4 (Mario standing under the mushroom ? block, live $006D/$0086 = 1/79 = level x ≈ 335, screen x 185) jump into the block; the mushroom emerges with $39 = 0. WHILE it is still on the block, write_memory CPU $0039 = 2 and step 3 frames - the item redraws as the starman (tiles $8D/$E4) and a pickup would set the star timer. NOTE: writing $0039 = 2 BEFORE the bump does not survive - the block-spawn code at CPU $BC6B-$BC79 rewrites $0039 from $0756 (0 for small Mario), so the change must be made after the hit while the item is emerging. $0039 is not otherwise written anywhere in PRG (only writer = CPU $BC79).
rows.why: the starman rises out of the block in this screenshot; OAM $8D and $8D(h) (the star's upper point) over $E4 and $E4(h) (its lower half), palette 6 attr $63: rendered from sprite CHR they make the five-pointed star
